title: Restored Atlas Returns to the Bookseller's Window
summary: A repaired binding reveals marks that an earlier owner concealed.
author: Books and Objects Desk
paragraphs: An atlas of early observatory engravings has returned to Mr. Corven's window after six months with the binder. The repair has exposed a narrow strip of manuscript beneath the rear board, previously hidden by a later lining.

The strip carries three station names and a set of figures, but no date or signature. Mr. Corven believes it was used as waste paper when the atlas was first bound; the binder considers that judgment possible but not certain.

Several plates in the volume are familiar from later editions. Their borders, however, were cut before those editions appeared, and a comparison of the paper marks may help establish which impressions came first.

The atlas is available for inspection but has not been priced. Readers are reminded that a fragment found inside a binding may be interesting without being an authority for the charts printed beside it.
